institutional_aggregates.note: These are sector aggregates, not named institution-by-institution holdings.

primary_dealers.frequency: Weekly; updated Thursdays with the previous week's data
primary_dealers.note: Dealer positions are aggregate net positions reported by primary dealers, not a list of each dealer's holdings.

extended_holders.note: These are Federal Reserve Financial Accounts sector aggregates, not named-firm holdings.

nport.note: SEC Form N-PORT bulk files are hundreds of MB and are ingested by a separate quarterly workflow rather than the daily updater.

security_intelligence.note: CUSIP matching combines SOMA positions with recent Treasury auctions and, when the quarterly N-PORT cache is available, fund holdings. A missing match does not mean no other holder owns the security.
security_intelligence.audit_note: Security rows identify which source blocks contributed each match and add time-to-maturity / auction-recency fields derived from source dates. A recent-auction match is issuance context, not proof that the auction award is still held by any current owner.

change_leaderboard.note: Periods differ by source: countries are monthly, sectors quarterly, and primary-dealer series weekly.

government_accounts.note: Detailed federal and trust-fund investments in Government Account Series and other federal securities. API dollar balances are normalized to billions; category totals and Grand Total are excluded from the leaf-line sum to reduce double-counting.

ownership_shares.note: Each share uses a Debt to the Penny denominator from the same observation date, or the latest business day on or before it. Categories still should not be summed because source definitions and valuation bases differ.

soma_concentration.note: Maturity buckets are calculated from the CUSIP-level SOMA sample stored in the dashboard (top positions), so they are a concentration view rather than a full maturity distribution.

unusual_change_alerts.method: A change is flagged when it clears a source-specific absolute dollar floor and is either at least 2.5× the median absolute change in the available history or at least 10% versus the previous observation. High severity begins at 4× the historical median or 20%. This is a statistical screening rule, not a prediction.
